content:
We need propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: step1 (forward) amide formation from carboxylic acid + amine (coupling). So retrosynthetic step: break amide bond to give carboxylic acid (or activated) and aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). The amide is C(=O)N attached to an aniline (c3ccccc3N). So disconnection: target -> precursor1: aromatic aldehyde? Wait amide formation is forward: carboxylic acid + amine -> amide. So retrosynthesis: cut C=O-N bond to give carboxylic acid (or acid derivative) and amine. The amide carbonyl is attached to the phenyl ring (c3ccccc3N) as N attached to carbonyl, and the carbonyl attached to the alkene chain (C=C) attached to aromatic sulfonyl phenyl. So the acid precursor would be something like: /C=C/C(=O)OH attached to aromatic sulfonyl phenyl? Actually the amide carbonyl is part of the chain: .../C=C/C(=O)N... So the acid precursor would be the α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid: /C=C/C(=O)OH attached to the sulfonyl phenyl. So we need a precursor: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2)cc1 (the acid). That's plausible.

Second step: Doebner modification to form the α,β-unsaturated acid from aromatic aldehyde and malonic acid. So retrosynthesis: the unsaturated acid precursor can be derived from aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) attached to sulfonyl phenyl? Actually the aldehyde would be the aromatic ring bearing sulfonyl group and aldehyde at para position relative to sulfonyl? In target, the sulfonyl phenyl has substituent /C=C/C(=O)N... So the aldehyde precursor would be same phenyl with aldehyde instead of the unsaturated chain: c2ccc(CHO)cc2 attached to sulfonyl group. So precursor2: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(CHO)cc2)cc1.

Third step: sulfonamide formation from aniline (the first phenyl with methyl) reacting with sulfonyl chloride derived from sulfonyl phenyl? Actually sulfonamide formation: amine (aniline) + sulfonyl chloride -> sulfonamide. In target, the sulfonamide is between the first phenyl (with methyl) and the sulfonyl phenyl. So retrosynthesis: break S-N bond to give aniline (first phenyl with methyl) and sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2-Cl) where Ar is the second phenyl (with aldehyde or unsaturated acid). So precursor3: aniline: Cc1ccc(NH2)cc1 (p-toluidine). And sulfonyl chloride: ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(CHO)cc2 (or with acid later). So we have three steps: 1) sulfonamide formation, 2) Doebner modification to create α,β-unsaturated aldehyde? Wait Doebner gives unsaturated acid from aldehyde, malonic acid. So we need aldehyde precursor. So step order retrosynthetic: target -> break amide (step A) -> unsaturated acid + aniline (c3...). Then break unsaturated acid to aldehyde + malonic acid (but we don't need malonic acid as reagent, just aldehyde precursor). Then break sulfonamide to aniline and sulfonyl chloride.

Thus we need to find templates for each disconnection.

We have template for sulfonamide formation (reverse direction). The search gave template ID 733 etc. That template is retro: product is sulfonamide, reactants are sulfonyl chloride + amine. So we can use that.

We need template for Doebner modification (retro: product is α,β-unsaturated acid, reactants are aldehyde + malonic acid). Not sure if template exists. Could search for functional groups broken: "carboxylic acid" and formed "C-C double bonds". But we need to specify broken: "carboxylic acid" (since decarboxylation?) Actually forward Doebner: aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid + CO2. So retro: unsaturated acid -> aldehyde + malonic acid (with CO2). So broken functional groups: "carboxylic acid" (one of the carboxylic acids broken) and formed "C-C double bonds". Let's search with those groups.
